title: sporadic-tail-latency-scratch-jasper
content:
Quick snapshot (handnote) - do not share outside eng-runtime channel

What happened
- Observed sporadic p99 tail latency spikes on hosted inference for model: redwood/gpt-small-v1 (quantized) between 02:58-03:30 UTC on 2026-03-11. Visible in per-route dashboard as ~120ms baseline, spikes to 1.6s at p99. Not consistent across requests; roughly 1 in 350 requests.
- Spike window maps to a handful of Dedicated GPU hosts (rack-07, host ids: gpu-07a, gpu-07b) but also saw a few hits on shared serving pool.

Immediate checks I ran (copying commands so I don't forget):
- curl /v1/requests (replay) with same prompt id (from logs):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RWD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-small-v1","input":"Summarize: test jitter"}' | jq .latency_ms
- grabbed raw trace for request ids: r-1a2b3c4d5e -> attached to Linear RT-4823.
- ps aux + strace on worker (ssh gpu-07a) while slowly replaying traffic (local loadgenerator) to see syscall stalls. Nothing obvious: no long syscalls, no IO wait spikes.

Hypotheses (ranked rough):
1) Intermittent KV cache eviction + re-warm for hot context windows > ~2k tokens causing kernel path to fallback + extra memcpy overhead.
2) Background checkpoint/metric flush thread causing mutex contention in the allocator (jemalloc stats enabled on those hosts recently).
3) Network path hiccup to GPU host (brief retransmits) causing RPC layer retry/backoff visible as occasional long tail.
4) CPU stealing during host-level maintenance (kube node cordon/uncordon) at the time window.

What made me lean to hypothesis #1:
- Spikes correlate with long prompt sequences (many are chat history replays, median seq_len at spike ~2100).
- Traces show a sudden delta in "KV lookup" op time (trace span ~500ms extra on some spikes).
- gpu memory graphs show slight transient bump in host GPU mem allocations at the same time.

Quick repro plan (min-effort):
- Reproduce on a dedicated host iso: replay 10k requests with a distribution skew (90% short 64 tokens, 10% long 2k+ tokens) and measure p99.
- Experiment flags: --kv-cache-size=4GB vs 8GB, --prefer-hot-kv-copy=true (runtime flag, see PR #2114).
- Run with jemalloc stats off (env MALLOC_CONF).

Commands I will run next (ordered):
1) ssh gpu-07a -> sudo systemctl stop metric-flush.service && restart worker to get clean baseline.
2) ./tools/loadgen --model redwood/gpt-small-v1 --mix "short:90, long:10" --concurrency 16 --duration 20m --out ./results/spike-test-20260311.log
3) run profiler on a subset: ./bin/serve --profile-sampling=1ms --profile-output=profiles/trace-jasper-1.pb && run single long request, collect stack.
4) toggle KV flags: EDITOR=vim ./configs/docker-run.env (set KV_CACHE_LIMIT=8g), restart and compare.

Notes for debugging traces
- Look for span named "kv_lookup" -> contains timing and key size. Filter traces where kv_lookup > 200ms.
- Also search for "allocator_lock" spans; if present, correlate with jemalloc stats in /var/log/alloc.json.

Temporary mitigations for customer impact
- If reproducible, create policy to route long-context requests to dedicated capacity with larger KV cache (temp rule route:long-context -> dedicated-highmem).
- Add circuit-breaker: if p99 > 1s for >2m on a route, switch to compressed-context fallback (drop oldest messages) and record eval.

Open questions / TODOs (my next week plan)
- [ ] Run the mix replay on gpu-07a/07b and a control host (gpu-03a) and save full perf counters. (assigned to me)
- [ ] Confirm jemalloc stats were enabled on those hosts on 2026-03-11 (ask infra: @Mina).
- [ ] If KV re-warm implicated, implement a micro-benchmark to measure copy costs of large kv segments (priority med).
- [ ] Add automatic trace sampling for long-context requests (if not already). (ops ticket)
- [ ] Validate if PR #2114 (prefer-hot-kv-copy) changes behavior in loadgen; pair with Ethan for a quick run.

Random scribbles / hypotheses to revisit
- Maybe cache fragmentation causes lookup to do sparse reads across memory pages -> TLB pressure; could explain non-CPU syscall stalls. Need perf top + meminfo during spike.
- The spikes sometimes line up with small GC-like pauses in Python heaps on manager process (rare). Check timeline of manager GC and worker span correlation.

Contact list to ping
- Mina Patel (infra) - jemalloc + host history
- Ethan Cole (perf) - run loadgen + profiler pairing tomorrow morning 09:00 PT
- Zoë Kim (PM) - potential customer impact if we require route change

Notes_to_self:
- Keep this doc alive while I run the experiments. Move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/investigations once we have clear repro.
- Save raw perf outputs to gs://redwood-inference-perf/spikes/2026-03-11/ with prefix jasper-

End log.

-- jasper
